questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Talking to people who doubt climate change
Why Florida is getting hotter every year
How to recycle plastic litter at home
Why scientists disagree about climate change
questions.why: Rob says they'll find out how to talk with people who doubt the science of global warming.

questions.q: What happened to Sarah Ott when she was at college?
options: She started a climate campaign with her friends
She moved away from Florida to study in New York
She began to doubt climate change, like others
She became a science teacher at a local school
questions.why: Surrounded by people who didn't believe climate change was real, she slowly started to doubt it too.

options: She is a BBC reporter covering the weather
She teaches children climate science
She works for a big oil company in Texas
She studies psychology at university
questions.why: She works as a climate campaigner, teaching children the science behind climate change.

questions.q: What distinction does Marco Silva make?
options: Between scientists and the journalists who report them
Between young people and old people
Between Americans and Europeans
Between the ill-informed and real deniers
questions.why: He distinguishes being ill-informed from being a full-blown climate denier.

questions.q: Why might some people not understand climate science, according to Marco?
options: The facts can be quite complex
Nobody explains it on TV
Scientists keep changing their minds
It is not taught in schools
questions.why: He says the facts can at times be quite complex, quite dense.

questions.q: Which way of persuading an ill-informed person is mentioned?
options: Telling them that their ideas are stupid
Refusing to talk to them until they change
Sharing stories of how the weather changed
Showing them only numbers and graphs
questions.why: Sam says you might share personal stories of how the weather has changed or ask why they doubt the evidence.

questions.q: According to Professor Sander van der Linden, what happens if you insult a climate denier?
options: They change their mind quickly and apologise
They hold on to their views more strongly
They stop talking about climate altogether
They ask for more information and evidence
questions.why: Marco says if you confront them, people will hold on to their views even more firmly.

questions.q: What do the presenters say is needed instead of confrontation?
options: More laws against climate deniers
Louder campaigns
Less talk about science
Understanding, empathy and patience
questions.why: Sam says what's needed is understanding and empathy, and patience to show fact from fiction.
